'''Reginald Jamaal Evans''' (born May 18, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played in the [[Big3|Big3 League]]. A [[Power forward (basketball)|Power forward]], Evans played 13 seasons in the NBA with seven teams. Evans was known for his rebounding, tenacity and hustle on the defensive end.

== College career ==
Evans attended Coffeyville Community College in [[Coffeyville, Kansas]] from 1998 to 2000 and then transferred to the [[University of Iowa]]. In 2001, he led the nation in free throws attempted, [[free throw]]s made, and [[double-double]]s. He also led the [[Big Ten Conference]] in rebounding and double doubles in 2001 and 2002, was named [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten Tournament]] [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] in 2001, second-team All-Big Ten in 2002, and Honorable Mention All-American in 2001.

== Professional career ==

=== Seattle SuperSonics (2002–2006) ===
Evans signed with the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] as a free-agent in 2002, where he became known for his tenacious rebounding. In 2004–05, he led the league in rebounds-per-minute-played after finishing in the top 10 the two previous seasons. Despite playing under 24 minutes per game, he finished ninth in the NBA in total rebounds. A 2005 statistical analysis published on [[ESPN]] determined that on average, Evans will rebound one quarter of all shots missed while he is in a game. In the 2006 season this dipped to 21.5 percent, however, this was still good enough to edge out teammate [[Marcus Camby]] for the best rebound rate in the NBA.

Evans made the news on December 6, 2005, when he was absent for the opening minutes of the second half in a loss to the [[New York Knicks]]. Circumstances did not allow Evans to take a [[anabolic steroid|steroid]] test prior to the game, so a league official required that it be done at halftime. Evans laughed off the suggestion he was under suspicion. "I've been clean since I've been in the league. I've been clean since I've been in college. I've been clean since I've been in high school, middle school, elementary school. I'm just cleaner than clean. I'm cleaner than [[Pine-Sol]]."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2251638 |title=ESPN – NBA to stop in-game drug testing after Evans delay – NBA |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=December 7, 2005 |access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref>

Evans's best statistical season came to a halt on January 3, 2006, when the Sonics front office dismissed head coach [[Bob Weiss]] and promoted assistant [[Bob Hill]] to replace him. In Hill's new system, Evans lost his starting spot and his minutes were drastically reduced.
[[File:Korver cropped.jpg|thumb|Evans defends against [[Kyle Korver]]]]

=== Denver Nuggets (2006–2007) ===
On February 23, 2006, the Sonics traded Evans to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Nuggets Acquire Patterson, Evans, Smith In Four-Team Deal | url = http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/patterson_evans_trade_022306.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = February 23, 2006 | access-date = July 12, 2010}}</ref> In his first five games with the division-leading Nuggets, Evans played more minutes than he did in his final 21 games with the Sonics.

On March 10, 2006, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Evans had zero points but 20 rebounds. Evans became the first player with 20 rebounds in a scoreless game since [[Dennis Rodman]] did it for Chicago on December 15, 1997, against Phoenix.

During a 2006 game, Evans yanked [[Los Angeles Clippers]] center [[Chris Kaman]] by the [[testicles]] in an attempt to gain a position advantage. Kaman immediately pushed Evans to the floor and later said, "I felt I got a little violated by another man."<ref name="ESPN06">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2428627 |title=Kaman: Evans pulled testicles, prompting outburst |last=ESPN.com news services |date=May 1, 2006 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 7, 2009}}</ref><ref name="LATimes">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-cliprep1may01-story.html |title=NBA Investigates Kaman Incident |last=Reid |first=Jason |date=May 1, 2006 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |pages=print edition D-8 |access-date=January 7, 2009}}</ref> However, Kaman ultimately decided not to press assault charges against Evans. Evans was fined $10,000 and a [[flagrant foul]]-two for his actions.<ref name="Transactions">{{cite news |url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9F00EFD9113FF931A35756C0A9609C8B63&scp=2&sq=reggie+evans+chris+kaman&st=nyt |title=Sports: Transactions |last=Hawkins and P David Lonie. |date=May 2, 2006 |publisher=New York Times, The |access-date=January 7, 2009}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2007–2009) ===
On September 10, 2007, he was traded along with the draft rights to [[Ricky Sanchez]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Steven Hunter]] and [[Bobby Jones (Washington Huskies)|Bobby Jones]].<ref>{{cite web | title = 76ers complete trade with denver nuggets | url = http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/evans_trade_070910.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = September 10, 2007 | access-date = July 12, 2010}}</ref>

Evans was put in as the starting [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] for the Sixers [[2007–08 NBA season]]. He took the Sixers from the worst rebounding team, to the top 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/statistics/sortable_team_statistics/sortable2.html?cnf=1&prd=1#top |title=NBA.com |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref> He missed only one game the whole season, and started more games than in his two with Denver. During game three of the Sixers' first round playoff series against the [[Detroit Pistons]], Evans scored 9 points and grabbed 5 rebounds en route to a Sixers' victory amidst chants of "Reg-gie! Reg-gie!" from the Philadelphia fans at the [[Wachovia Center (Philadelphia)|Wachovia Center]].

=== Toronto Raptors (2009–2011) ===
On June 9, 2009, Evans was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Jason Kapono]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Raptors Acquire Evans From Philadelphia | url = http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/evanspr_060909.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = June 9, 2009 | access-date = June 15, 2009}}</ref> Evans started the season with a foot injury and did not play a game for the Raptors until February 10, 2010.
On November 24, 2010, Evans pulled down a then-career high 22 rebounds (along with 12 points) in the Raptors' 106–90 win over the Philadelphia 76ers.

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2011–2012) ===
On December 22, 2011, Evans signed a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://losangeles.sbnation.com/los-angeles-clippers/2011/12/22/2656441/reggie-evans-los-angeles-clippers-2011-nba-free-agency |title=NBA Free Agents 2011: Los Angeles Clippers Sign Reggie Evans – SB Nation Los Angeles |date=December 22, 2011 |publisher=Losangeles.sbnation.com |access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref> He would finish the season with an average of 1.9 points and 4.8 rebounds in 13.8 minutes per game over 56 games,<ref name="yahoo1">{{cite web|author=Adrian Wojnarowski |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--nets-land-reggie-evans-in-sign-and-trade-deal.html |title=Nets land Reggie Evans in sign-and-trade deal – Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date=May 30, 2012 |access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref> becoming a fan favorite along the way for his physical style of play.<ref>{{cite web|author=Eric Patten |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/catching-reggie-evans |title=CATCHING UP WITH REGGIE EVANS |date=March 23, 2013 |work=nba.com |access-date=April 21, 2024}}</ref>

=== Brooklyn Nets (2012–2014) ===
[[File:Reggie Evans Nets.jpg|thumb|Evans with the Nets in 2013]]
On July 11, 2012, Evans was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in a sign-and-trade deal.<ref name="yahoo1" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Evans_Trade_Release_120711.html |title=NETS: Brooklyn Nets Acquire Reggie Evans |work=Nba.com |date=July 11, 2012 |access-date=August 3, 2012}}</ref> On November 21, 2012, he became the first NBA player to be fined for [[Flop (basketball)|flopping]] after a 95–90 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/story/gameon/2012/11/21/reggie-evans-fined-flopping/1720499/ Nets' Reggie Evans first player fined for flopping]</ref> One league executive had called Evans "the star" of flopping in a preseason demonstration video.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--source--nets--reggie-evans-first-nba-player-to-be-fined-for-flopping-225031651.html Source: Nets' Reggie Evans first NBA player to be fined for flopping<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

While Nets player [[Kris Humphries]] was out with an injury, Evans was given the opportunity to start. He remained in the starting lineup afterwards, as the Nets decided to start Evans over Humphries.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nets start Evans over Humphries|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/nets/evans_starts_over_humphries_r2Ib5yU2gU7kSPWO3ohwKI|work=nypost.com|publisher=New York Post|date=December 10, 2012}}</ref> On March 27 in a game against the Portland Trail Blazers, Evans notched career highs in both points (22) and rebounds (26) as the Nets won 111–93. 2 days later in a game against the Denver Nuggets, Evans had another great night with 15 points and 16 rebounds but the Nets lost 109–87. Evans said he heard a teammate say to Nets coach [[P. J. Carlesimo]] to bench Evans because of lack of offensive production. Evans used this as inspiration to be more aggressive on the offensive end of the floor.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/reggie-evans-attributes-fantastic-month-teammate-call-him-173601997--nba.html Reggie Evans attributes his fantastic month to a teammate's call for him to be benched]</ref> In his first season with the Nets, Evans played 80 games with 56 starts, and for the second time in his career, he averaged over 10 rebounds a game with 11.1.

=== Sacramento Kings (2014–2015) ===
On February 19, 2014, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] traded Evans and guard [[Jason Terry]] to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for guard [[Marcus Thornton (basketball, born 1987)|Marcus Thornton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-jason-terry-and-reggie-evans|title=KINGS ACQUIRE JASON TERRY AND REGGIE EVANS|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 19, 2014|access-date=February 19, 2014}}</ref>

Having only played in nine of the Kings' first 16 games to start the 2014–15 season, and having not played in the previous seven games, Evans made up for the absence of starting center [[DeMarcus Cousins]] against the Memphis Grizzlies as he recorded 17 points on 7-of-10 shooting and 20 rebounds in 35 minutes off the bench. The seldom-used Evans sparked Sacramento back into the game during the third quarter, getting [[Marc Gasol]] in foul trouble and slicing Memphis' lead to 74–65 heading to the fourth. However, the Kings went on to lose the game, 97–85.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141130/MEMSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Grizzlies beat Kings 97–85 for 5th straight win|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 30, 2014|access-date=December 1, 2014}}</ref>

Evans' final NBA game was played on April 10, 2015, in a 103 - 116 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he recorded 1 rebound and 1 steal.

=== BIG3 Basketball ===
In 2017, Evans joined the [[BIG3]] basketball league's [[Killer 3's]] team, playing alongside [[Charles Oakley]] (who also was the head coach), [[Chauncey Billups]], and [[Stephen Jackson]].
In 2018, Evans joined the [[BIG3]] basketball league's  [[3 Headed Monsters]], playing alongside [[Rashard Lewis]], [[Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf]], and being coached by [[Gary Payton]].
